title: Daynori Production Hosting Options & Capacity Modeling

limitations.limit: 750 free instance hours shared across ALL services per month
limitations.failureMode: Two active services (Web + API) consume 1,488 hours/month. Free quota expires in ~15.6 days, causing guaranteed complete service blackout for the rest of each month.

limitations.limit: Spins down after 15 minutes of inactivity
limitations.failureMode: Takes 50 to 75 seconds to wake up. First request times out; intolerable for real active users.
Next.js SSR and V8 memory heap easily spike past 512MB under concurrent load, triggering unhandled OS OOM kills.
1,000 active users producing daily notes, tasks, journals, and sync receipts consume ~5-10MB/day; 500MB cap exhausted in 50-100 days.
Connection exhaustion ('53300: too many connections') under 50+ concurrent sync requests.

limitations.limit: Projects paused after 7 days of inactivity
limitations.failureMode: Manual operator intervention required to unpause; zero SLA.
RPO > 24 hours; data loss risk in event of schema corruption or hardware failure.

currentFreeTierAudit.verdict: COMPLETELY UNVIABLE FOR PUBLIC PRODUCTION SERVICE. Suitable strictly for zero-cost developer rehearsal and isolated previews.

options.name: Option 1: Modern Managed PaaS (Recommended)

web.specs: Global Edge CDN, serverless SSR, automatic image optimization, 1TB bandwidth, instant atomic git deployments, edge middleware.

apiAndWorker.specs: 2 dedicated container services (API: 2 vCPU, 2GB RAM; Worker: 1 vCPU, 1GB RAM), zero cold starts, health checks, automatic horizontal scaling.

databaseAndAuth.specs: Dedicated micro/small compute, 8GB high-speed NVMe storage (auto-expanding), 100,000 MAU Auth, Supavisor connection pooler (200 pooled connections), 7-day Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR), daily automated offsite backups.

storage.specs: $0 egress fees, $0.015/GB storage, S3 API compatibility, globally distributed object caching.

dnsAndSecurity.specs: DDoS protection, TLS 1.3, HTTP/3, Web Application Firewall (WAF), rate limiting, DNSSEC.

monitoring.specs: Crash reporting, performance tracing, uptime monitoring, synthetic health checks with alerting.

strengths: Zero cold starts, instant interactive responsiveness
Automatic edge distribution for global static and PWA assets
Robust enterprise-grade database backups with 7-day continuous PITR
Minimal DevOps overhead allowing focus on application features
Clear, linear scaling economics as user base grows
tradeoffs: Slight vendor coupling to Vercel/Railway platforms

options.name: Option 2: Unified Container Cloud (DigitalOcean / AWS Light)

webApiWorker.provider: DigitalOcean App Platform (or AWS App Runner)
webApiWorker.specs: 3 containerized components (Web: Basic 1GB RAM @ $12; API: Professional 2GB RAM @ $25; Worker: Basic 512MB RAM @ $5).

database.specs: 1 vCPU, 2GB RAM, 25GB storage, built-in connection pooling, automated daily backups.

auth.provider: Supabase Auth / GoTrue self-hosted or Supabase Pro

strengths: Single administrative dashboard and consolidated invoicing
Private internal VPC networking between API and database
tradeoffs: Slower global frontend distribution than Vercel edge
Requires manual container tuning and Dockerfile maintenance

options.name: Option 3: Lean Bare-Metal / Dedicated VPS (Hetzner + Coolify)

computeServers.provider: Hetzner Cloud (2× CPX31 instances in Falkenstein/Nuremberg)
computeServers.specs: Server 1: 4 vCPU, 8GB RAM, 160GB NVMe (Web, API, Worker, Reverse Proxy); Server 2: 4 vCPU, 8GB RAM, 160GB NVMe (PostgreSQL 16, PgBouncer, Redis).

orchestration.specs: Self-hosted PaaS with automated SSL, webhook deployments, and container monitoring.

storageAndOffsiteBackups.specs: Encrypted offsite WAL archiving and logical dumps via pgBackRest/Restic.

capacityMetrics.devopsEffort: High (Requires Linux sysadmin, OS security patching, manual firewall rules)

strengths: Maximum compute and RAM per dollar (16GB RAM, 8 vCPU total for ~$35/mo)
Zero vendor lock-in; 100% portable Docker containers
tradeoffs: No managed SLA for database failover; manual disaster recovery responsibility

recommendation.rationale: Option 1 provides the ideal balance for Daynori's initial public release: it completely eliminates cold starts and memory crashes, provides enterprise-grade 7-day continuous PITR database backups, offloads global asset caching to Vercel's edge network, and requires virtually zero ongoing sysadmin maintenance. It allows the core team to focus on application reliability, user support, and feature validation rather than server patch management.
